items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-21
items.q: David L. Herman is identified only as the Notary Public who administered the oath for Alice Kern's affidavit regarding Dominic J. La Rocca. The interviewee (Dominic J. La Rocca) does not mention David L. Herman in his testimony or narrative.

ctx.x: Susu Ramis played guitar Willie guitar played bass Harry Nunez played violin and I played the comic we played in the downtown section that is way down below Elysian Fields Avenue now this is 19 2 3 and 4 and 5 no night I made ahead I went ahead of my statement 19 3 4 and 5 and maybe 6 the uptown band I played with a boy named George Gieffer George Gieffer bass Joe Taranto guitar Freddie Inglot this boy sells ice cream around the streets today violin and Nick LaRocca this group this group and all the above groups…

came and appeared, Mrs. Alice, how do you pronounce her? Alice, Alice Kern. Alice Kern, K-I-E-R-N. A female person over the age of majority and full well known unto me notary public, who first being duly sworn, disposed and said as follows, that deponent was well acquainted with and has personally known for more than 25 years, one Dominic J. La Rocca, who resides in the city of New Orleans, state of Louisiana. A deponent is an organist by profession and during a period of time from 1914 to 1916, set down on paper…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: I kept corresponding with the man to see if I could get some more out of him.

ctx.x: Well, he wrote down to Mr. Howard Jacobs. He put a piece in the paper for asking for an old time jazz band to write him. That he was trying to clear up the great mystery that hangs over the jazz. That someone should get credit where it should be. Now many people ask, amongst this one was this Tom Brown and the record changer. Well, now these things I had never known before, the record changer, the claims that Brown made. These had just come to my mind. Now when you have a family to support you, just don't jump up…

It says, uh, CCE, DJ LaRocca, number 2218 Constant Street. October the 14th, 1957, I see. Heading of the letter, Mr. Harry V. Sushant, comma, President, New Orleans Jazz Club, comma, 2417 Octavia Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. Dear Harry, colon, for many months now, comma, I have delayed writing you concerning a matter, a matter, that I know means a great deal to you and the members of your organization, period. This matter means a great deal to me, comma, personally, comma, because one of the principal…
Now read Sushant. I'm reading it. I don't want to know them.
